description: The Australian Mine Waste Database holds mine waste features across Australia, such as tailings storage facilities and waste rock dumps, with waste name, waste type, waste status, storage type and location, linked to the associated mineral deposit, its commodities and a deposit model adapted from the Critical Mineral Mapping Initiative classification (Hofstra and others, 2021). Where available it adds structure type, volume and rehabilitation status. The DataCite and data.gov.au pages say it is compiled from published references and public information such as company reports by Geoscience Australia under the Exploring for the Future programme, and that it is reached through the Atlas of Australian Mine Waste on the Geoscience Australia Portal. The DataCite record (version 2.0, created 30 March 2023) gives a CC BY 4.0 licence, so it is free to reuse, while data.gov.au lists the licence as not specified. Coverage is national. Caveats: download formats and the number of features are not stated on the pages read, and volumes are only filled where published. For simulation it maps tailings and waste stores that are hazard sources for dam failure, dust and acid drainage scenarios, and secondary resources for critical mineral supply models. Related catalogue records include the Global Tailings Portal, the Australian mine production dataset and the OZMIN mineral deposits database.
